description: (TL;DR: I'm posting my CMU 15-150 lectures on the internet for free, at https://lnkd.in/grVynCDy) The end is here. Being in a teaching environment is one of a kind, and coming back for the course that I love was an opportunity I will never forget. Thank you to all my TAs, all the people who supported me, to Semgrep for sponsoring the course, and to my wonderful students, who put up with me as we navigated the (surprisingly less than you would think) scary world of functional programming. I will not forget you. I consider it my mission in life to teach functional programming, and I'm just getting started. I'm thrilled to announce that the reason for this post being so late is that I have posted my lectures from this summer, for free, online! You can find all the materials at my website, here: https://lnkd.in/grVynCDy All my love, I put into this course. ## Sign in to view more content. title: Jacob Neumann - Teaching
description: I served as a teaching assistant for this course six times, three of them as the "Head TA". Unlike most courses, the homework assignments in 150 are made by the TAs, so as Head TA I would supervise groups of several TAs as they revised a homework assignment (and wrote new problems, as needed) and developed test cases for "auto-grading" the student's code submissions. My main duties included delivering the lectures (I delivered 22 of the course's 28 lectures), coordinating the TA staff (we had 23 TAs that semester), and attending to our 100+ students. I returned to teach 15-150 once again for the Summer 2021 term, as the sole instructor (assisted by 15 excellent TAs). Upon returning to the course in 2021, I began work on the smlhelp auxiliary library, which has grown to include several modules, some including numerous functions and hundreds of lines of code.
